paper_title: The Unseen Targets of Hate -- A Systematic Review of Hateful   Communication Datasets
caption: Monolingual vs. multilingual datasets over time. While monolingual datasets are more frequent, around 2017 researchers began producing multilingual datasets.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the number of hateful communication datasets published annually from 2012 to 2022, categorized by the number of languages they support: monolingual (1 language, represented by blue bars) and multilingual (2+ languages, represented by orange bars). The horizontal axis displays the years in chronological order from 2012 to 2022, while the vertical axis represents the number of datasets on a logarithmic scale, ranging from 10⁰ (1) to 10² (100), with major tick marks at 10¹ (10) and 10² (100). For each year, two bars are shown side-by-side: the blue bar for monolingual datasets and the orange bar for multilingual datasets. From 2012 to 2016, only monolingual datasets are present, with their numbers gradually increasing from approximately 1 in 2012 to around 10 in 2016. In 2017, multilingual datasets first appear, with approximately 5 datasets, while monolingual datasets reach about 20. From 2018 onward, both types increase, with monolingual datasets peaking at over 100 in 2021 and multilingual datasets reaching around 20 in 2020 and 2021. In 2022, the blue bar is lighter in color and appears to represent a value of approximately 30, while the orange bar is very small, around 1–2. The chart visually demonstrates that monolingual datasets have consistently outnumbered multilingual ones, but the latter began to emerge around 2017 and have grown in number since then.
